decision.proposal: Adopt a versioned capability and connector contract with typed resolve, invoke, and reconcile operations. Resolve an unresolved request against a pinned resource registry snapshot before final authorization; invoke only the exact resolved effect under its bound authorization envelope; reconcile a persisted intent after possible external commit. Express preparation, commit observation, and meaningful cancellation as explicit phases or typed results. Fabric owns authorization, durable outcome classification, receipts, and reconciliation scheduling; connectors provide bounded execution and evidence and cannot widen authority. Every admitted descriptor declares effect class, resource grammar, schemas, isolation and secret requirements, idempotency class, provider-key mapping, commit observation, retry boundaries, reconciliation support, and evidence profile; missing or contradictory declarations fail registration. Classify operations as pure/read-only, naturally idempotent, externally keyed, compensatable, non-repeatable, or unknown; compensation or reconciliation alone never makes an effect repeatable, and unknown consequential connectors cannot register. Derive and record provider replay keys from stable effect or operation identity, never ActionQueue AttemptId. Distinguish pre-dispatch failure, confirmed non-commit, confirmed commit, terminal provider failure, and possible commit. Persist possible commit as Uncertain and reconcile it without blind re-invocation; a later invocation requires evidence of non-commit and explicit policy permission. Bind connector implementation version and descriptor hash to authorization and receipts. ActionQueue remains the sole durable executor, with Fabric transaction and AQ attempt recovery handled across their separate stores.
